analysis.title: Global Equity Pulse: Beyond the Chips: Powering the AI Revolution (November 2026)
key_insights: TGI argues AI data-center growth depends on reliable electricity, so the investment opportunity extends beyond semiconductors to power generation, transmission, electrical equipment and cooling.
The IEA estimates global data centers used about 415 TWh of electricity in 2024 (about 1.5% of global consumption) and expects roughly 945 TWh by 2030, with AI the most important driver.
The IEA says US data centers could account for almost half of US electricity-demand growth through 2030.

EPRI estimates data centers could use 9% to 17% of US electricity by 2030, versus roughly 4% to 5% today. Its medium-growth scenario has US data-center consumption rising from about 184 TWh in 2024 to 596 TWh in 2030.

Power demand from AI is concentrated in large hyperscaler campuses. Some use more power than small states and may strain grids not built for rapid local demand growth. Developers may seek dedicated or behind-the-meter generation where the grid cannot expand fast enough.

TGI research points to strong demand for gas turbines, high-voltage equipment and other infrastructure tied to the data-center buildout. TGI expects a mix of renewables, natural gas and, over time, nuclear to meet demand.

TGI names three exposure areas: a leading US power provider (power generation), a Japanese supplier of power systems, semiconductors and advanced cooling for data centers (electrical equipment and cooling), and specialized Asian power-management suppliers. No companies are named.
One Asian power-management company reported 70% y/y growth in AI-related businesses in Q1 2026 and expects AI products to be about 30% of its 2026 revenue mix.

TGI stresses selectivity and price discipline. A favorable theme does not make every power-related company attractive, especially where enthusiasm is already in valuations, and AI investment must generate acceptable returns.

Outlook: TGI is relatively positive. It sees a robust global economy despite inflation headwinds and higher rates, healthy Q3 earnings growth, and AI infrastructure demand as the top earnings driver. It also flags elevated valuations, persistent profitability concerns and financing issues, and expects market performance to broaden as investors diversify away from AI.

October market review: global equities were broadly unchanged. US and Europe rose modestly, while Asia Pacific, emerging markets and Japan declined. Value clearly outperformed growth as investors cut crowded AI, semiconductor and momentum positions. US small caps improved relative to mega-cap tech toward month-end.

sector_views.rationale: TGI sees an attractive long-term opportunity in a leading US power provider because rising data-center and commercial electricity demand and grid investment could support capital spending and earnings growth.
TGI sees opportunity in suppliers of power systems, turbines, transformers, high-voltage equipment and cooling as AI raises power density.
TGI says investors are reducing exposure to crowded AI and semiconductor positions, and it prefers the less visible parts of the AI value chain while stressing valuation discipline.

earnings_insights: Corporate earnings growth continued in Q3 2026 and looks healthy for the full year, per TGI. AI infrastructure demand is the top earnings driver.
An unnamed Asian power-management company reported 70% y/y growth in AI-related businesses in Q1 2026 (reported) and expects AI-related products to be about 30% of 2026 revenue (company expectation).
